note: Edward Hopper's life, kept to what a named source states. Every entry carries the source that says it and a link to that page; nothing here is written from memory, and where two sources disagree the entry says so rather than choosing quietly. This is a reminder for somebody reading a dated ledger leaf — not a biography, and not a substitute for one. From 2026 the black notebook of Josephine Hopper, transcribed on this site, is one of the sources: what it states is quoted in her words and linked to the page she wrote it on, and the pictures and journeys in it are as often hers as his.

events.what: The house in Nyack that his maternal grandparents built — Hopper’s home until 1910.
Born in Nyack, New York, thirty miles up the Hudson from Manhattan.
Begins commuting into the city to study at the New York School of Illustrating.
Enrols at the New York School of Art; studies under William Merritt Chase, and prefers the classes of Robert Henri and Kenneth Hayes Miller.
Begins supporting himself as a commercial artist and illustrator — work he will go on doing for about twenty years. The first three decades of Book IV are its record.
First of three extended stays in Paris, the last of them in 1910; he begins painting out of doors.
Last of the Paris visits. Nyack ceases to be his primary residence.
Sells his first canvas, at the Armory Show.
Moves to the apartment at 3 Washington Square North where he will live and work until his death. The inside front cover of Book I gives that address.
« E.H. came in 1913 », in her list of the tenants of number 3 from Glackens on. Her year-by-year chronicle, kept backwards from 1961 to 1906, leaves 1913, 1912 and 1911 blank.
Begins the printmaking that runs into the early 1920s — the etchings that fill the first forty leaves of Book I.
Josephine Verstille Nivison joins the Washington Square Players.
First solo show, at the Whitney Studio Club. He is thirty-seven.
In Gloucester, Massachusetts, meets Josephine Verstille Nivison.
Marries Jo Nivison. From here she keeps the record: “Recorded by Jo N Hopper (Mrs. Edward Hopper) at time each work is finished, or before it leaves studio.”

The Frank K. M. Rehn Galleries begin to represent him, and go on doing so for the rest of his career. “Frank K. M. Rehn” first appears in Book IV in November of this year and then recurs for forty years.
« Gloucester. Honeymoon. Watercolors. Chicago August. » — the first joint year of that chronicle; every year before it is hers alone.
« got car - Dodge », with the summer at Two Lights in the Coast Guard cottage, then Ogunquit and Charleston. Page 116 calls it « the Dodge - 1" car ».
The Whitney Studio Club closes, to make way for the Whitney Museum of American Art.
“Early Sunday Morning” is acquired within months of being finished, and becomes part of the Museum’s founding collection.
First Cape summer: « Cape - Wellfleet then Bird's Cage S. Truro » — the rented Bird's Cage, three summers before they built.
The Whitney Museum of American Art opens, and first acquires his work.
Included in the first Whitney Biennial, and in twenty-nine further Biennials and Annuals down to 1965.
« Cape - last yr. at Bird's Cage. Bgt. land. »
Builds a second home and studio on Cape Cod, and keeps it for the rest of his life. The Truro and South Truro watercolours in Books I and III begin here.
« Cape - Built house. » Her one line for the year, and the whole of it.
« Cape Huricane », in her spelling, with a second visit to the Slaters in Vermont. In March, four days of his cold with the temperature taken hour by hour — « E.H. 1938. », pages 107 to 125.
« Trip West - Calif., Oregon, Wyoming. »; the forward chronicle of page 44 gives it as « Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Frisco, Portland, O. - Cape », with « Columbia R. » in the margin.
“Nighthawks”, his most acclaimed composition.
First Mexico: « Mexico - City, Saltillo, Sept. Monterrey », « by R.R.! », « no Cape ». Page 48 lists every Mexican journey to 1957 under the heading « To get this straight ».
« Xmas 44 E. elected to Instit. of Arts + Letters »; « Cape - ap. Salmagundi Prize ».
« Mexico - Sattillo Grand Titon Cape. », with « Buick 39 » in the margin — the second Mexico, by car.
« # 3 invasion by N.Y.U. » — the whole of the year's line, and the beginning of the Washington Square fight that fills two of the other notebooks.
« Group of 6 or 7 paintings at Rehn. very successful. » Then, in February, « N.Y. Hospital - Prostate », the Grosvenor Hotel after it, « Stayed into May », and « 3 trips to N.Y. Hos. hemmorhages ».
The Whitney organises his second career retrospective. Leaf 2 of Book I is headed with a note of it.

« Retrospective Ex. Hopper, Man of the Year at Whitney Mus. - W. 8" St. E. in hospital at opening of Exhib. » The show goes on to Boston and Detroit, and in Chicago « E. degree D.F.A. » at the Art Institute, « stayed at Palmer House. + parties ».

« Mexico - Sattillo in heat wave. On to Santa Fé + return to Cape - began efforts for Electric. » The backwards chronicle puts the Chicago degree here: « E. gets degree Dr. of Fine Arts - Chicago Art Inst. »

« Dec. 7 or 6 off for Mexico - via El Paso, TX. + South. Stay at Guanacinato (Posada de la Presa », in her spelling — after « Water Color Show at Metrop. » and, in September, « By air to N.Y. for Metrop. jury ».

« from Guanajuato - middle of Jan on to Mitla, Oaxaca », « Feb. on to Puebla », Monterrey, and « back to N.Y. Mar. 1" in time for jury duty at Virginia Mus. at Richmond »; « Whitney Annual Oct. 53 Fire Escape ».
« S. Truro. E. N.Y. Hos. hernias - Feb. »; Gloucester in September « trees », and Frank Rehn.
« Dec. 6" 1956 H. H. + Pacific Palisades » until June 6, 1957 — page 47 gives the address as « H. H. F. Pacific Palisades, Calif. », and the initials are not expanded here.
« N.Y. Hos. Jan. 29, 58 », then « burglar Feb. 11", 58 » — the burglary page 3 may allude to in « from trunk in basement (burglars) ».
« Moved to Greenwich Gallery - 71 Washington Place - Mar. 1958 » — her dealer, not his. The notebook lists her group show there, the four hundred announcements she sent, and who came.
« T.V. performance at Boston Mus. Ap. 10, 1961 », « E. H. + J. H. », at the Sheraton Plaza; « Tape recorded in N.Y.C. - Sat. Ap. 29, 61 » with Brian O'Doherty.
A second Whitney retrospective in his lifetime, organised by Lloyd Goodrich — a lifelong friend, and the donor of four of these six ledgers.
Last of the Whitney Biennials and Annuals he takes part in.
Dies in the studio at 3 Washington Square North. Book IV’s final entry is dated 23 March.
Jo Hopper dies ten months after Edward, having been hospitalised. Their artistic holdings — nearly three thousand items — are bequeathed to the Whitney.
The Whitney publishes the catalogue raisonné, twenty years in the making. It was made from these books.

disputed.about: When he took the top floor of 3 Washington Square North
disputed.what: The Whitney's artist page says he lived and worked in the same Washington Square apartment from 1913 until his death; other chronologies give 1929 for a move to the top floor of the building. Both may describe the same tenancy at different scales. Only the Whitney's wording is used above, because mixing two sources into one sentence is how a date nobody stated gets published. Her black notebook adds a third voice: the list of the tenants of the house on page 117 says « E.H. came in 1913 », while her own year chronicle leaves 1913 blank.

disputed.about: When Chicago gave him the degree
disputed.what: The black notebook says it twice. Page 45's forward chronicle puts « Chicago Art Institute - E. degree D.F.A. » after the Detroit leg of the 1950 retrospective; page 20's backwards chronicle lists « E. gets degree Dr. of Fine Arts - Chicago Art Inst. » under 1951. Both are hers, and both stand above under their own year.

Page 19 of the black notebook has « Boston Mus. T.V. Ap. 20 (N.Y. Mar. 29) »; page 61 has « Ap. 10, 1961 », the stay at the Sheraton Plaza « Sat. Ap. 8 - Mon. Ap 10" », and the tape « recorded in N.Y.C. - Sat. Ap. 29, 61 ». The fuller page is the one quoted above; the other is not corrected.
